name: Fairy Meadows
description: A high meadow facing the north face of Nanga Parbat, reached by jeep from Raikot Bridge and a short trek.
lead: A high meadow under Nanga Parbat, reached by a jeep track and a morning’s walk

image.alt: First sunlight on the summit of Nanga Parbat above the Raikot glacier and the pines of Fairy Meadows

overview.headline: A high meadow facing the north face of Nanga Parbat
paragraphs: Fairy Meadows is a grassy clearing in the pines at about 3,300 m, looking straight across the Raikot Glacier at Nanga Parbat, the ninth-highest mountain on earth.

Getting there is half the story: a narrow jeep track from Raikot Bridge on the Karakoram Highway, then a walk of two to three hours. There are no roads at the top, only wooden cabins, a few camps and the mountain.

seasons.text: Snow lingers on the trail into May, and the cabins open late in the month.
Green meadows and the clearest views of the mountain. Days 15–20°C, nights near freezing.
Crisp, clear days in September. The cabins close in October as the cold sets in.
The meadow lies under deep snow, and the jeep track is closed.

gettingThere.byRoad: From Raikot Bridge it’s an hour by jeep to Tato, then a walk of two to three hours. Jeeps run from June to September.
gettingThere.byAir: Flights to Gilgit save little time, as the jeep track starts on the Karakoram Highway. We go by road.

notes.title: The walk in
notes.text: Two to three hours uphill from Tato on a good path. Ponies can carry bags, or you.

notes.title: The jeep track
notes.text: Narrow and high above the gorge. Local drivers only; it is a white-knuckle hour for some.

notes.title: Cold nights
notes.text: At 3,300 m nights drop close to freezing, even in July. Bring warm layers and a torch.

notes.title: No signal
notes.text: There’s no mobile signal at the meadow, and power only in the evenings.
